findings.title: 'Integrate now' silently threw away 8 of 9 subs and presented the 1-frame result as a finished master, with no error, warning or count anywhere in the UI
findings.what_happened: With 9 accepted 300s subs, clicking 'Integrate now' produced a master card reading 'M51 - L / 1 frame - 00:05:00 integration - L' and no other feedback: no toast, no error banner, no 'x of y subs rejected' line. The database shows integrated_master_frames has 1 accepted row and 8 rows with rejection_reason 'registration failed: too few stars to register: reference=0, frame=N, need >= 3', and integrated_masters.stats_json is {"framesIntegrated":1,"framesRejected":8,...}. Two distinct failures compound: (a) the integrator picked sub 1 as the alignment reference, detected 0 stars in it, and then failed every other sub against that empty reference instead of choosing a different reference or aborting; (b) the count of dropped subs exists in the outcome and in the DB but is never rendered for a manual integration.
findings.expected: Two things. (1) A reference frame with 0 detected stars must not be accepted as the reference -- fall back to the next-best frame (frames 4-9 each detected 29-30 stars) or abort with 'could not find a usable reference frame'. (2) Integration must report its own result: 'Integrated 1 of 9 subs - 8 failed to register' with the reason, exactly as the automatic-integration path already does (auto_integration_service.dart:378 builds precisely that sentence). Losing 89% of a night's data must never be silent.
findings.repro: 1. Seed 10 lights for one session with real FITS star fields (star sigma 1.0-2.25 px). 2. Analytics > History > Audit Night A > sparkles. 3. Workbench > 'Reject HFR above' at 3.5 (leaves 9 accepted). 4. Scroll the right column to Integration settings, click 'Integrate now'. 5. Wait ~40 s. 6. Read the Masters card and look for any error surface.
findings.evidence: UI after the run: Masters card 'M51 - L / 1 frame - 00:05:00 integration - L' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-24.png), header still '9 accepted - 1 rejected', no toast (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-21.png). DB: sqlite3 skotiq.db "select image_id,accepted,rejection_reason from integrated_master_frames where master_id=2" -> 1|1|(null) then 8 rows 0|'registration failed: too few stars to register: reference=0, frame=4..30, need >= 3'. stats_json {"framesIntegrated":1,"framesRejected":8}. App log: '[STAR_DETECT] Detected 0 stars after filtering' on the reference frame.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/session_review_controller.dart:710 integrate() -- the returned outcome is stored in state.lastOutcome but workbench_view.dart:190 uses it only for a preview path and a button label; framesIntegrated/framesRejected are never rendered. Reference selection is in the native post-session integration path.
findings.proposed_fix: In integrate(), after the outcome returns, if outcome.result.framesRejected > 0 raise a warning toast + a persistent banner on the master card carrying the count and the most common rejection_reason; reuse auto_integration_service.dart's existing summary builder. Separately, make reference selection reject a candidate with fewer than the minimum registrable stars and retry with the next candidate before failing the run.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end. I restored session 1 to the finding's exact state (header '9 accepted · 1 rejected', panel 'Will integrate 9 accepted subs using Winsorized sigma') and pressed Integrate now. Result: master id 14 with stats_json {"framesIntegrated":1,"framesRejected":8,"rmsResidual":0.0,"totalIntegrationSec":300.0} and 8 integrated_master_frames rows reading 'registration failed: too few stars to register: reference=0, frame=4|11|29|30, need >= 3'. UI afterwards: Masters card 'M51 · L / 1 frame · 00:05:00 integration · L', header still '9 accepted · 1 rejected', and the entire accessibility tree contains no error, warning or rejected-count node for that run. Cause is nailed down further than the finding states: the reference is audit_L_001.fits, the sub with the brightest near-saturated star (57952 ADU), which the app's detector scores 0 stars on while my independent peak finder reads 40 well-separated stars; with that sub culled the same button integrates 7 of 7 at 0.11 px residual. Reporting half verified structurally: session_review_controller.dart:710 integrate() is exact; workbench_view.dart:190 'final outcome = state.lastOutcome' is exact and consumed only at :193 for previewPath; MasterPreviewView.fromOutcome (master_preview_view.dart:33-42) is the ONLY widget rendering '${r.framesIntegrated} frames · ${r.framesRejected} rejected' and its sole caller is ab_compare_panel.dart:284, while the workbench master card at workbench_view.dart:353 uses MasterPreviewView.fromMaster whose stat line has no rejected term.

findings.title: The cull rail advertises 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' from a curve it already knows is stale; pressing it always refuses, and its advice ('re-integrate to refresh') reproduces the same stale curve
findings.what_happened: The improvement curve is derived from the master that was just produced. Because that master contained only 1 registered frame (see the P0 above), the persisted curve has one point and a recommendation of {keepN: 1, predictedSnrGainPct: 0.0, reason: 'Keep all 1 subs: already optimal (+0.0% SNR vs full stack)'}. The cull rail then renders an enabled primary action 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' whose tooltip is 'Drop to the optimizer-recommended best 1 subs (+0% SNR)'. Pressing it three times changed nothing (still 9 accepted in the DB) and toasted 'Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling'. So the control knows the curve does not match the 9 accepted subs, yet still renders a specific, quantified, actionable label -- and its remedy is to re-run the same integration that produced the stale curve.
findings.expected: The rail must decide staleness at render time, not at press time. When the curve's population does not cover the currently-accepted subs, or when predictedSnrGainPct <= 0, show a disabled/absent action (or an explicit 'analysis out of date' chip) rather than a confident 'Keep best 1 (+0%)'. A control should not offer an operation it will unconditionally refuse.
findings.repro: 1. Do the Integrate-now repro above (produces a 1-frame master). 2. A new button 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' appears beside Blink mode / Select-lasso. 3. Click it. 4. sqlite3 skotiq.db "select count(*) from captured_images where session_id=1 and is_accepted=1" -> still 9; toast reads 'Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-21.png, rsr-22.png, rsr-25.png show 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' while the header reads '9 accepted - 1 rejected'; AT-SPI tree after the click contains 'panel: Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling'. DB improvement_curve_json for master 2: {"points":[{"n":1,...}],"recommendation":{"keepN":1,"keptIndices":[0],"predictedSnrGainPct":0.0,"reason":"Keep all 1 subs: already optimal (+0.0% SNR vs full stack)"},"population":[".../audit_L_001.fits"]} -- population length 1 vs 9 accepted, which is exactly the staleCurve guard in session_review_controller.dart:1377.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/widgets/sub_cull_rail.dart:473 (tooltip) and :475 (label 'Keep best $keepN (+${gainPct}%)'); guard in session_review_controller.dart:1354 cullToRecommended()
findings.proposed_fix: Lift the population-vs-accepted comparison out of cullToRecommended() into a getter the rail reads while building, and gate the button on it plus predictedSnrGainPct > 0.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The render-time/press-time asymmetry is exactly what the current source does, and the two cited widget lines are exact. sub_cull_rail.dart:274 passes the action through whenever `curve != null && curve.recommendation.keepN > 0` -- no population check, no gain check -- and :470-480 renders an enabled primary SkotiqButton labelled 'Keep best $keepN (+${gainPct.toStringAsFixed(0)}%)' (:475) inside a Tooltip 'Drop to the optimizer-recommended best $keepN subs (+…% SNR)' (:473). Every staleness test lives in the press handler instead: SessionReviewController.cullToRecommended() returns CullToRecommendedResult.staleCurve when the curve's population length differs from the accepted set, when paths duplicate, or when any population path is no longer accepted, and alreadyOptimal when keepN >= population.length. So in those states the control can only ever be pressed to be refused while still advertising a specific quantified action. This is NOT contingent on the P0 that produced the 1-frame master: any accept/reject after an integration diverges the population, and the alreadyOptimal case renders a '+0%' button that also refuses. Not re-driven live (needs a session with real FITS subs, which the scratch profile has none of); the source is unambiguous.
findings.location_wrong: cullToRecommended() is at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/session_review_controller.dart:1418-1480 in the rebuilt tree, not :1354 (the file grew 66 lines in the fix wave); sub_cull_rail.dart:473/475 are exact.
findings.closure_evidence: VERIFIED CLOSED at source by lead: sub_cull_rail.dart:289 now passes `onCullToRecommended: _offer.isOfferable ? () => _cullToRecommended(_offer) : null`, so the action is disabled rather than advertised-then-refused.

findings.title: Project-growth panel groups subs by UTC calendar day, so one continuous evening is reported as two nights and every night is dated a day late
findings.what_happened: Session Review (narrative) 'This project over time' reports '2.0h integrated - 24 frames across 4 nights' with x-axis labels Jul 26 / Jul 28 / Jul 29 / Jul 30, and 'Best night: Jul 28 - 0.5h'. The database contains exactly THREE observing sessions (Audit Night A on the evening of Jul 25 local, B on Jul 27 local, C on Jul 29 local). Audit Night C is one continuous 50-minute run (19:30-20:20 America/New_York) that straddles 00:00 UTC, and the panel splits it into two separate 'nights' (Jul 29 with 4 frames, Jul 30 with 4 frames). Every other night is also labelled with the following calendar day because 21:00 EDT is 01:00 UTC.
findings.expected: Nights should be grouped by OBSERVING night in the site's local time (the conventional noon-to-noon boundary), so three sessions produce three points labelled Jul 25, Jul 27, Jul 29 and the panel says '3 nights'. Never a UTC calendar day: for any observer west of Greenwich the label is a day late, and for any observer east of Greenwich (all of Europe/Asia) the 00:00 UTC boundary falls in the MIDDLE of the observing night, splitting every single night in two.
findings.repro: 1. Seed three sessions of M51 lights, the third spanning 19:30-20:20 America/New_York on 2026-07-29 (crosses 00:00 UTC). 2. Analytics > History > Audit Night A > sparkles (Review & Integrate). 3. Scroll the narrative view to 'This project over time'.
findings.evidence: UI: '2.0h integrated - 24 frames across 4 nights', axis Jul 26 / Jul 28 / Jul 29 / Jul 30, 'Best night: Jul 28 - 0.5h' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-08.png). DB: sqlite3 skotiq.db "select strftime('%Y-%m-%d',captured_at,'unixepoch') utc, strftime('%Y-%m-%d',captured_at,'unixepoch','localtime') local, count(*) from captured_images group by 1" -> 2026-07-26|2026-07-25|10, 2026-07-28|2026-07-27|6, 2026-07-29|2026-07-29|4, 2026-07-30|2026-07-29|4. Three local nights, four UTC days.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/smart_project_service.dart:679 _dayOf() -> DateTime.utc(dt.year, dt.month, dt.day); used by growthCurve(), bestNight() and reReferenceAdvice()
findings.proposed_fix: Group by observing night, not UTC date: shift the timestamp by the site's UTC offset and then by -12h before truncating to a day (the standard 'noon-to-noon' night key), and label the point with that local date. bestNight() and reReferenceAdvice() share _dayOf and are wrong in the same way -- a European user's 'best night' is currently the better HALF of a night.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim in the running app. Session Review > Narrative > 'This project over time' renders '2.0h integrated · 24 frames across 4 nights', 'Best night: Jul 28 · 0.5h', axis Jul 26 / Jul 28 / Jul 29 / Jul 30. Ground truth from the DB: three observing sessions (Audit Night A 2026-07-25 21:00, B 2026-07-27 21:00, C 2026-07-29 19:30 local America/New_York); master 1's 24 accepted subs group as 2026-07-26|10, 2026-07-28|6, 2026-07-29|4, 2026-07-30|4 by UTC day but 2026-07-25|10, 2026-07-27|6, 2026-07-29|8 by local day. Audit Night C is one continuous 19:30-20:20 local run and 20:00 EDT is exactly 00:00 UTC, so it is cut in half. I also saw the day-late half in isolation earlier: with a single-night master the panel read '1 frame across 1 night' labelled 'Jul 26' for a session whose header reads '2026-07-25 21:00'. Cited location exact: smart_project_service.dart:679 _dayOf returns DateTime.utc(dt.year, dt.month, dt.day); its one call site is :583 in _foldedSubs (captureDate), feeding growthCurve (:279-287) and _meanWeightByNight (:606-607) behind bestNight (:318). The finding also names reReferenceAdvice (:341); it shares _foldedSubs but I did not verify it consumes captureDate, so treat that third consumer as unconfirmed.

findings.title: Narrowband mixer 'Apply palette' is a dead control: no composite, no file, no error, no log line
findings.what_happened: With three finalized single-filter masters for the target (Ha 20 frames, OIII 15, SII 10), the Narrowband mixer renders correctly, SHO/HOO presets populate the weight matrix correctly, and 'Apply palette' is enabled. Pressing it five times (three via click-img, twice via a raw xdotool click on the hovered button) produced nothing at all: narrowband_composites stayed at 0 rows, no FITS was written anywhere on disk, no toast appeared in the accessibility tree on six consecutive polls, and the app log recorded no combine activity. The screen's toast path is demonstrably alive -- the same session surfaced 'Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling' from the cull rail -- and the neighbouring 'Run both' A/B button responded immediately with a 'Preview...' state and native STAR_DETECT log lines, so neither the toast machinery nor the click mapping explains the silence.
findings.expected: Apply palette should either produce a narrowband_composites row plus an on-disk composite FITS and render it in the composite card, or fail loudly with the reason ('Need at least two finalized narrowband masters to combine.' is already written for that case). Silently doing nothing on the mixer's only action makes the whole SHO/HOO feature untestable by the user.
findings.repro: 1. Seed three finalized integrated_masters for the target with filter Ha / OIII / SII and real master_fits_path files. 2. Session Review > Workbench > Refresh. 3. Scroll to 'Narrowband mixer', press SHO (matrix fills SII->R, Ha->G, OIII->B correctly). 4. Press 'Apply palette'. 5. sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select count(*) from narrowband_composites' -> 0; no new .fits under the masters output dir; no toast.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-30.png (mixer with 3 channels), rsr-33.png (SHO matrix + enabled Apply palette), rsr-35.png (cursor hovering the button, confirming the hit target). AT-SPI polls immediately after the click contain only 'panel: Combine matrix' -- no error node. DB: narrowband_composites count 0 after 5 presses. Log tail contains nothing between the click and the next discovery sweep.
findings.proposed_fix: Instrument runNarrowband with an entry log and surface every exit path (including the <2-input guard) through the same toast the cull rail uses; then fix whichever leg is swallowing the call. The button should also show a busy state while combiningNarrowband is true, which would have made the no-op visible.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with a control experiment that rules out the obvious false-positive explanations. Four presses of 'Apply palette' (including one clicked dead-centre after re-measuring from a fresh screenshot, because an A/B progress bar had shifted the layout) produced: narrowband_composites still 0 rows, no new .fits under the masters output dir, no error/composite node in the accessibility tree over six consecutive polls, no toast in a screenshot taken 1.0 s after the click, nothing in the app log. Click mapping proven good: a click 120 px below the same button, on 'Run both', fired immediately and produced 15+ native '[STAR_DETECT] ... Detected 29 stars' lines plus a visible 'Preview... 100%' bar. Preconditions satisfied: three finalized masters (Ha 20 / OIII 15 / SII 10) with on-disk master_fits_path files, and NarrowbandChannelRef.fitsPath comes straight from m.masterFitsPath (controller :366-370), so runNarrowband's 'inputs.length < 2' early-out with its error toast cannot fire. Cited chain matches source with small drift: workbench_view.dart:304 exact, runNarrowband declared at :1233, combineChannels at post_session_seam.dart:326-333 (finding says :327). CAVEAT: I could not pin which link is broken — the button's onPressed never invoking onApply, or bridge.apiCombineChannels never returning (invisible because SkotiqButton here is built without isLoading, so combiningNarrowband:true shows no spinner). Dart-side logging does not reach app.log in this build, so log silence does not discriminate. Do not fix one link on faith.

findings.title: The 'Maximum Quality' integration profile is a placebo -- it produces byte-identical settings to Balanced
findings.what_happened: Selecting each of the five integration profiles in turn and diffing the whole ADVANCED block of the accessibility tree: Fast changes the resampler to Bilinear, Few Subs changes rejection to Percentile clip with 0.2/0.1, Long Night / Gradient changes normalization Mode from Global to Local grid -- but Balanced and Maximum Quality produce an IDENTICAL 30-line block (`diff bal.txt maxq.txt` is empty) and an identical summary sentence. The source confirms it: IntegrationSettings.preset(maximumQuality) sets resampler=lanczos3, weighting=snrSquared, generateRejectionMap=true, cosmeticCorrection=true, outputBitDepth=f32 -- every one of which is already the constructor default that balanced inherits. The only field that differs between the two presets is sourcePreset, which is a label.
findings.expected: A profile named 'Maximum Quality' must actually cost something in exchange for quality -- e.g. a tighter RANSAC threshold, more reference stars, local normalization, linear-fit/percentile rejection tuned for the sub count, or drizzle. As shipped, a user who deliberately picks Maximum Quality over Balanced for their best data gets exactly the same stack and is misled about it.
findings.repro: 1. Session Review > Workbench > Integration settings > expand Advanced settings. 2. Click 'Balanced', capture the ALIGNMENT..DRIZZLE block of `drive_linux.py tree`. 3. Click 'Maximum Quality', capture again. 4. diff -> no differences. 5. Repeat for 'Long Night / Gradient' -> exactly one line differs (Global -> Local grid), proving the capture method detects real changes.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/bal.txt vs /tmp/ns-audit/maxq.txt -> identical (30 lines each); /tmp/ns-audit/bal.txt vs /tmp/ns-audit/ln.txt -> 1 line differs. Summary line unchanged: 'Will integrate 9 accepted subs using Winsorized sigma. Recommends culling the worst 10%.' for both. Source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/imaging/integration_settings.dart:737-745 vs the constructor defaults at :672,:676,:690,:691,:692.
findings.proposed_fix: Give maximumQuality settings that actually differ (e.g. ransacThresholdPx 1.5, maxRefStars 120, normalization local, reject linearFit) -- or drop the chip. Also make the panel's one-line summary mention the knobs the chosen profile changed, so three profiles cannot render the same sentence.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Read the current source. integration_settings.dart:737 is exactly `case IntegrationPreset.maximumQuality:` returning const IntegrationSettings(resampler: lanczos3, weighting: snrSquared, generateRejectionMap: true, cosmeticCorrection: true, outputBitDepth: f32, sourcePreset: maximumQuality). All five are already the constructor defaults (:670 lanczos3, :674 snrSquared, :688 true, :689 true, :690 f32), and balanced at :733 is `const IntegrationSettings(sourcePreset: balanced)` i.e. all defaults. The two objects therefore differ only in sourcePreset, and the only non-test consumer of sourcePreset anywhere in packages/ or apps/ is integration_settings_panel.dart:51 `active: _s.sourcePreset`, which decides which chip is highlighted. findings.title: Stack & Share byte-swaps every pixel when 'Apply calibration' is on (the default), so it reports 'Reference frame has only 0 stars' and cannot stack anything
findings.what_happened: With 8 accepted 300s L subs whose FITS provably contain 40 well-separated stars each (peak 40614 ADU over a 440 ADU background, sigma 22 ADU -> SNR ~1800), pressing Start in Stack & Share fails instantly with 'Failed to initialize stacker: Reference frame has only 0 stars, need at least 5 for alignment'. Turning OFF the 'Apply calibration' switch and pressing Start again on the SAME frames initialises fine -- the log reads 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars'. The two paths differ only in how the pixels reach the stacker: calibration-off uses the native file loader (stacking_start_from_file), calibration-on loads the frame into Dart via apiReadFitsLinearData and hands back a u16 buffer (stacking_start_from_data). The bridge's image_data_to_linear_f64 decodes the ImageData buffer with u16::from_be_bytes, but fits.rs wrote that buffer with to_le_bytes (as does every other reader in the imaging crate -- processing.rs, calibration.rs, registration.rs, stretch.rs, star_reduction.rs, background_extraction.rs and lib.rs all use from_le_bytes). Every pixel therefore comes back byte-swapped: a 440 ADU background becomes 0xB801 = 47105 and a 40614 ADU star becomes 0xA69E = 42654, so the background spans ~42000-52000 with ~10000 ADU of fake noise and the stars are buried. Hence zero detections. 'Apply calibration' is ON by default, so out of the box Stack & Share fails 100% of the time on 16-bit FITS -- the format every camera writes.
findings.expected: apiReadFitsLinearData must decode ImageData with the same endianness fits.rs encoded it with (little-endian). Stack & Share with the default options must stack the session's frames.
findings.repro: 1. Have a session with 8 accepted 16-bit (BITPIX=16, BZERO=32768) light FITS. 2. Imaging > Stack > Stack & Share. 3. Leave all options at their defaults and press Start -> 'Reference frame has only 0 stars'. 4. Toggle 'Apply calibration' OFF and press Start -> stacker initialises with 34 stars (it then fails later for an unrelated reason, see the residual finding). 5. Verify the frames really have stars: python3 peak-finder over audit_L_017..024.fits reports 40 local maxima each, top fluxes ~37000-40000 over a 440 median with sigma 22.
findings.evidence: UI: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-09.png shows 'Apply calibration' ON with 'Stack & Share failed / SkotiqError.imageError(field0: Failed to initialize stacker: Reference frame has only 0 stars, need at least 5 for alignment)'; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-10.png shows the same dialog with the toggle OFF. App log (/tmp/ns-audit/r-science-review/app.log): three 'Starting live stacking from data: 512x512 (262144 pixels)' entries that each ended in the 0-stars error, then '14:53:10 Starting live stacking with reference: .../audit_L_024.fits' followed by 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars'. Independent pixel check of audit_L_017.fits: median 440, MAD-sigma 22.2, 40 local maxima, brightest 40614.
findings.where: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:1537-1560 image_data_to_linear_f64 (from_be_bytes for U16/U32/F32/F64) vs native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/fits.rs:322-365 (to_le_bytes). Reached from packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_and_share_service.dart:724 _loadRawU16 -> stacking_engine_seam.dart:172 apiReadFitsLinearData.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the four decodes in image_data_to_linear_f64 to from_le_bytes, and add a round-trip unit test (write a known FITS, read it back through api_read_fits_linear_data, assert the pixel values match). The same bug silently corrupts two science surfaces: default_science_backend.dart:856 (the Dart fallback for per-frame science quality metrics, which then writes science_frame_quality_metrics / science_tile_metrics) and default_science_backend.dart:890-892 (computeLineRatios reads Ha/OIII/SII this way, so every BPT line ratio is computed on byte-swapped pixels), plus stretch_pipeline_service.dart:34.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live against session 3 (M51, 8 × 300 s L, BITPIX=16 BZERO=32768). Stack & Share opens with 'Apply calibration' ON; Start with untouched defaults gives 'Stack & Share failed / SkotiqError.imageError(field0: Failed to initialize stacker: Reference frame has only 0 stars, need at least 5 for alignment)' and the log shows 'Reading FITS linear data: .../audit_L_024.fits' ×2 then 'Starting live stacking from data: 512x512 (262144 pixels)'. Flipping ONLY that toggle off and pressing Start on the same 8 frames gives 'Starting live stacking with reference: .../audit_L_024.fits' then 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars'. Root cause verified in source exactly as stated: fits.rs:322-365 encodes with to_le_bytes for BITPIX 16/32/-32/-64 while bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:1530-1561 image_data_to_linear_f64 decodes U16/U32/F32/F64 with from_be_bytes. Arithmetic matches the symptom: background 440 ADU = 0x01B8 → LE [B8,01] → BE read 0xB801 = 47105; a 40614 ADU star = 0x9EA6 → [A6,9E] → 0xA69E = 42654, i.e. stars end up DARKER than the swapped background, hence 0 detections. Independent pixel check of audit_L_024.fits: median 420, MAD-sigma 22.2, 40 peaks, max 40916. Location correct, with one addition for the fixer: image_data_to_linear_f64 has a SECOND caller, api_compute_fits_quality_maps at imaging.rs:2235, so the same byte-swap corrupts the FITS quality-map endpoint too — wider blast radius than the finding states.

findings.title: A single sub that fails alignment aborts the entire Stack & Share run and deletes the partial result, even though the code counts 'rejected' frames as a normal outcome
findings.what_happened: With 'Apply calibration' off the stacker initialised on audit_L_024.fits with 34 stars, then the very first follower frame (audit_L_018.fits) was rejected for alignment residual and the whole run died: the dialog showed 'Stack & Share failed', no stacked_results row was written, and the log shows 'Live stacker stopped and resources released' one millisecond after the rejection -- frames 019-024 were never attempted. The native layer treats this as a per-frame rejection (it increments stats.rejected_alignment_failures and returns Err), and the Dart loop even has a framesRejected counter for exactly this case, but the counter is dead code: _addStackFrame is awaited without a try/catch, so the Err becomes an exception that escapes the for-loop into the run-level catch, which deletes the incomplete stacked_results row and rethrows.
findings.expected: A frame that fails to register must be counted and skipped, and the run must continue with the remaining subs -- exactly what the framesRejected counter was written for. Losing an entire night's stack to one satellite-trailed or wind-shaken sub is the single most expensive failure mode this feature has. The dialog should end with 'Stacked 6 of 8 subs - 2 rejected (alignment)'.

Watch the log: 'Adding frame to stack: .../audit_L_018.fits' then 'Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)' then 'Live stacker stopped'. 3. Dialog reads 'Stack & Share failed'. 4. sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select count(*) from stacked_results' -> unchanged (1, the pre-seeded row); no new row for this run.

findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_and_share_service.dart:328 (`final result = await _addStackFrame(...)` inside the followers loop, no try/catch) and the now-unreachable framesRejected accounting at :335-340; run-level catch that deletes the row at :484.

Surface the rejected count and the most common reason in the completion state.

With 'Apply calibration' off: 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars' / 'Adding frame to stack: audit_L_017.fits' / 'Frame 2 stacked (2 total, 0 rejected)' / 'Adding frame to stack: audit_L_018.fits' / 'WARN Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)' / 'Live stacker stopped and resources released' 1 ms later. findings.title: Registration reports a 10.34px alignment residual for a pure 2.2px translation of the same 40-star field, so even the working path cannot stack; match_radius_px defaults to 50px
findings.what_happened: audit_L_018.fits and audit_L_024.fits contain the SAME 40 stars offset by a rigid ~2.2px translation -- every star in 024 has a counterpart in 018 at distance 2.0-3.16px (median 2.24px), verified independently with a peak-finder and a nearest-neighbour match. The stacker matched 28 pairs and then computed an alignment residual of 10.34px, which exceeded its own 10.00px ceiling, so the frame was rejected. A correct affine fit on that geometry gives a sub-pixel residual. With match_radius_px defaulting to 50.0 and match_flux_tolerance to 0.7 in a 512x512 frame whose mean star separation is ~81px, the matcher is free to pair a star with a neighbour 50px away, and a handful of such wrong pairs is enough to wreck the least-squares fit and inflate the residual.
findings.expected: Registering two frames that differ by a 2.2px shift must produce a residual well under 1px and the frame must be accepted. Separately, max_alignment_residual_px = 10.0 is not a meaningful quality gate -- a 10px misalignment folded into the stack is a visibly smeared image; NINA/DSS-class tolerances are a fraction of a pixel.
findings.repro: 1. Stack & Share on the 8-sub session with 'Apply calibration' off. 2. Log: 'Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)'. 3. Independently measure the true offset: peak-find both FITS (40 peaks each) and nearest-neighbour match -> min 2.00px, median 2.24px, max 3.16px.
findings.evidence: App log 'WARN Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)'. Measured geometry: n024=40, n018=40, match distances min 2.0 / median 2.24 / max 3.16 px. Config defaults at native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stacking.rs:85-104.
findings.where: native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stacking.rs:91 match_radius_px: 50.0, :92 match_flux_tolerance: 0.7, :94 max_alignment_residual_px: 10.0; residual computed at :487 compute_alignment_residual and the fit at :485 compute_affine_transform.
findings.proposed_fix: Scale match_radius_px to the frame (e.g. a small multiple of the measured FWHM, or an iterative coarse-then-fine match seeded by a translation estimate) rather than a fixed 50px, and reject pairs whose residual is an outlier before the final fit (RANSAC / sigma-clipped refit). Then tighten max_alignment_residual_px to ~1px so the gate means something.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live and deterministically: two consecutive Stack & Share runs on the same 8 subs both logged 'Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)' for audit_L_018.fits against reference audit_L_024.fits, to the same 0.01 px. I measured the true geometry independently with my own FITS reader + peak finder + nearest-neighbour match (no app code): both frames contain 40 stars, every star pairs at 2.21-2.25 px, offset is a pure translation dx = -1.001, dy = +1.999 with per-star scatter 0.008/0.006 px — a rigid fit on correct pairs gives an essentially zero residual, so 10.34 px is ~5× wrong, not marginal. Config defaults cited are exact (stacking.rs:91 match_radius_px 50.0, :92 match_flux_tolerance 0.7, :94 max_alignment_residual_px 10.0) as are the fit/residual sites (:485, :487). CAVEATS: (a) I verified the transform math is self-consistent — compute_affine_transform is a standard Procrustes rigid fit and AffineTransform::apply at :272-276 applies exactly that transform — so the inflated residual cannot come from a fit/apply mismatch; that supports but does not prove the finding's 50 px-radius story. (b) 'even the working path cannot stack' is too strong: audit_L_017.fits (offset dx -2.0, dy -1.0) aligned and stacked fine in the same run, so the failure is per-frame. (c) An alternative cause to exclude before touching match_radius_px: bad CENTROIDS out of detect_stars would produce the identical observable, and the same detector returns 0 stars on audit_L_001.fits which my peak finder reads as 40 clean stars. (d) The real fix is likely a robust fit (RANSAC / iterative outlier rejection); tightening the radius alone would relocate the defect. Note the post-session integration path (registration.rs) reports 0.11 px on comparable frames, so this is specific to the live-stacker registration.
findings.severity_note: P1 (correct, but treat as P0 in combination with the Stack & Share abort finding — together they make the feature unable to finish a run)

findings.title: First Light's 'Could not load candidates' Retry button does not re-query -- the error survives Retry and a tab round-trip, and only a full app restart clears it
findings.what_happened: The First Light candidate list threw while decoding one row and rendered 'Could not load candidates / FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1) / tile-042' with a Retry button. I then fixed the offending value in the database (tile_id 'tile-042' -> 261982, confirmed typeof=integer) and pressed Retry twice, and switched to the Science sub-tab and back: the identical error text -- including the stale 'tile-042' fragment -- was still on screen. Only killing and restarting the app made the list load. The same staleness affects the success path: after the list HAS loaded, editing a detection's row (kind) outside the app and switching sub-tabs away and back still rendered the old value, so the candidate list is fetched once per app launch and is never refetched.
findings.expected: Retry must invalidate the provider and re-run the query -- that is the entire contract of a Retry button. And the candidate list must refresh as new detections arrive: the panel's own header promises 'Every solved frame is differenced against your deep sky atlas ... Anything that appeared, moved, or brightened on a deep patch lands here to review', which is false if the list is a one-shot read taken at app launch.
findings.repro: 1. Put a row in transient_detections whose tile_id is not parseable (SQLite type affinity permits a TEXT value in the INTEGER column). 2. Analytics > Science > First Light -> 'Could not load candidates'. 3. Fix the row: update transient_detections set tile_id=261982. 4. Press Retry -> same error. 5. Switch to Science and back to First Light -> same error. 6. Restart the app -> the candidate renders correctly.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-15.png (error state with Retry). AT-SPI tree after two Retry presses and a tab round-trip still contains 'panel: Could not load candidates' / 'FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1) tile-042'. DB at that moment: select id,tile_id,typeof(tile_id) -> 1|261982|integer. After a restart the same tab shows 'Possible unknown transient / 13h 29m 52.7s +47 11 43.1'.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/first_light/first_light_view.dart (candidate list provider + the Retry action on its error state)
findings.proposed_fix: Make Retry call ref.invalidate on the candidates provider (and make the provider watch the detections table as a stream, so new candidates appear during a run instead of at next launch). Separately, decode a row defensively so one unparseable row is skipped and reported rather than failing the whole list.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Symptom reproduced step for step. I set transient_detections.tile_id to the TEXT value 'tile-042' (SQLite affinity allows it), restarted, and Analytics > Science > First Light rendered 'Could not load candidates / FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1) / tile-042' with a Retry button. I fixed the row from outside the app (tile_id=261982, typeof integer), pressed Retry twice, and switched to the Science sub-tab and back: identical error text including the stale 'tile-042' fragment every time. Killing and restarting made the same tab render 'Possible unknown transient / 13h 29m 52.7s +47° 11' 43.1"'. TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) see location_wrong — Retry does call ref.invalidate, so the defect is downstream of it. (2) The finding's second claim — that an external row edit not appearing after a tab switch proves 'the candidate list is fetched once per app launch and is never refetched' — does not follow and I am NOT confirming it: the provider is a Drift watch stream, and Drift's stream store cannot observe writes made by a different process on the same file, so an unnoticed external sqlite3 edit says nothing about whether in-app detections push through. That sub-claim needs a re-test with an in-app write. Severity: the dead Retry is real, but the only demonstrated route into the error state is a value the app itself never writes, so P2 fits better than P1.
findings.location_wrong: The Retry action is NOT missing an invalidate. first_light_view.dart:406-410 already reads onPressed: () => ref.invalidate(firstLightCandidatesProvider). The provider being invalidated lives in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/transient_detections_provider.dart:138-152 — a StreamProvider returning transientDetectionsDaoProvider.watchRecentDetections(...), i.e. a cached Drift query stream. A fixer sent to first_light_view.dart will find a correct-looking Retry and may wrongly close this as a false positive; the broken link is that invalidating the provider does not produce a fresh execution of the underlying Drift stream.

findings.title: In the Submit-discovery dialog all three network chips are dead on a default install, and only the currently-selected network's blocker is explained
findings.what_happened: Submit discovery opens with Network = TNS and an amber line 'TNS submission needs your bot id/name, reporting group, data source, reporter, and api key -- configure them in Settings > Science.' Clicking the AAVSO chip does nothing (verified twice, once with coordinates measured from a cropped region shot so the hit point was unambiguous); TNS stays selected. Preview and 'Submit to TNS' are equally inert -- no dialog, no snackbar, no log line, no file. All three chips are disabled because _formatEnabled is false for each: AAVSO needs an observer code AND a magnitude zero point, MPC needs an observatory code AND a mover-class detection, TNS needs the five bot fields. None of the chips render a disabled affordance, and the panel prints a reason only for the format that happens to be selected, so a user who wants the AAVSO export -- the cheapest one to enable, it needs a single settings field -- gets a chip that silently ignores them and a message about TNS credentials that has nothing to do with their problem.
findings.expected: A disabled chip must look disabled and must say why on hover/press. Better: list all three networks with their individual status ('AAVSO - needs observer code', 'MPC - not a moving object', 'TNS - needs bot key') so the user can see at a glance which one is reachable and what it costs.
findings.repro: 1. Seed a confirmed newSource detection. 2. Analytics > Science > First Light > Submit. 3. Click AAVSO -> nothing; TNS stays selected (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-19.png vs rsr2-20.png are identical). 4. Click Preview -> nothing, no snackbar within 1s, nothing in the log.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-18.png (whole dialog), rsr2-19.png and rsr2-20.png (network row before and after an AAVSO click, byte-for-byte the same state). Source: transient_report_panel.dart:127-140 (`onTap: enabled ? ... : null`) and :142-148 (the reason block only renders _disabledReason for `_format`).
findings.proposed_fix: Render disabled chips at reduced opacity with a tooltip carrying that format's own _disabledReason, and show a per-format status list instead of a single reason line.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Verified in source at the cited lines and reproduced live. transient_report_panel.dart:127-140 renders the three chips with `onTap: enabled ? ... : null`, and :142-151 renders _disabledReason ONLY for the selected `_format`. _formatEnabled at :343-367 gates every format on d.reviewed, then aavso on aavsoAvailable + non-empty settings.aavsoObserverCode, mpc on a non-empty mpcObservatoryCode + a plausible-mover kind, tns on complete bot creds -- all false on a default install. skotiq_chip.dart:65-68 returns the bare chip when onTap is null: same fill, border and text colour as an enabled unselected chip, no Semantics, no cursor change, so a disabled chip is indistinguishable and silently swallows the tap. Preview/Copy at :296-320 are gated the same way. LIVE (profile v2-science-review, display :86): seeded one newSource detection, confirmed it (DB reviewed=1), First Light > Submit opens on TNS with the amber 'TNS submission needs your bot id/name...' line; clicking AAVSO changes nothing -- TNS stays selected and the TNS-specific reason stays on screen (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-12.png before, v2sr-13.png after).

findings.title: The Submit-discovery dialog defaults to TNS -- the live, irreversible, public submission -- rather than a local file export
findings.what_happened: The dialog opens with the TNS chip selected and the primary action reading 'Submit to TNS', with the footnote 'Submits live to the TNS via your bot API key -- creates a public AT record.' AAVSO and MPC, which write a file to disk that the user uploads themselves, are the non-default options.
findings.expected: Default to the reversible action. The first-listed and pre-selected network should be a local export (AAVSO), with TNS an explicit opt-in -- creating a public Astronomical Transient record on a mis-classified residual is not undoable, and a first-time user reaching this dialog has by definition never submitted anything before.

findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-18.png: TNS chip highlighted, primary button 'Submit to TNS', footnote 'Submits live to the TNS via your bot API key - creates a public AT record.'

findings.title: An unrecognised transient-kind token is presented to the user as a definite 'Dipole' artefact classification, which also silently blocks submission
findings.what_happened: TransientKind.fromWire falls back to TransientKind.dipole for any token it does not recognise. The candidate card then renders a 'Dipole' chip -- a specific, factual claim about the residual's morphology -- and Submit refuses with 'Dipole artefacts are not real transients - they cannot be submitted.' I hit this with a row whose kind was 'new_source' instead of the wire token 'newSource': the card asserted the detection was a dipole artefact and would not let it be reported. The fallback is deliberate and documented ('the least-exciting, artefact-leaning class'), but the UI presents the fallback as a measurement.
findings.expected: Keep the conservative gating, but label it honestly: an unknown token should render as 'Unclassified' and the refusal message should read 'This detection has an unrecognised classification and cannot be submitted', not assert a dipole morphology the differencing code never reported.
findings.repro: 1. Insert a transient_detections row with kind='new_source'. 2. Analytics > Science > First Light. 3. The card shows a 'Dipole' chip; pressing Submit toasts 'Dipole artefacts are not real transients - they cannot be submitted.' 4. Change kind to 'newSource' and restart -> the same row now reads 'New source' and Submit opens the dialog.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-17.png (card showing the 'Dipole' chip for a kind='new_source' row); AT-SPI snackbar 'Dipole artefacts are not real transients - they cannot be submitted.'; after the token fix the same card reads 'New source'. Source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/transients/transient_candidate.dart:45-50.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an `unknown` member to TransientKind, make fromWire return it, label it 'Unclassified', and gate submission on `kind == newSource || kind == pointBrightening || kind == movingStreak` rather than on `!= dipole`.

findings.title: Observing Alerts reports a First Light detection's brightness CHANGE as its apparent magnitude, so a self-discovered transient is announced as 'mag 2.4  NAKED EYE'
findings.what_happened: Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts renders the First Light detection as 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova - Unconfirmed - possible new transient / 13h 29m 52s +47 11' 43" / mag 2.4 [NAKED EYE]'. The detection row has delta_mag = -2.35 (a brightness CHANGE in magnitudes relative to the atlas template) and no photometric zero point anywhere in the pipeline -- there is no apparent magnitude for this object at all. transient_alert_mapper.dart:20 sets `magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs()`, and the card at transient_card.dart:581 then buckets `magnitude <= 6.0` as NAKED EYE, <= 10 BINOCULAR, <= 14 SMALL SCOPE. Because a difference-image delta magnitude of more than ~6 is essentially impossible, EVERY First Light self-discovery that has a measured delta is announced as a naked-eye or binocular object. The app is telling the user they have found a magnitude-2.4 supernova -- brighter than Polaris, and the brightest supernova in recorded history.
findings.expected: Do not populate the alert's apparent-magnitude field from a delta magnitude. Either leave magnitude null (the card already handles a null magnitude by omitting the chip) and show the delta separately as 'Δ2.35 mag', or compute a real apparent magnitude from a photometric zero point when one exists. The NAKED EYE / BINOCULAR / SMALL SCOPE bucketing must never run on a delta.
findings.repro: 1. Insert a transient_detections row with kind='newSource', delta_mag=-2.35, snr=18.4, reviewed=1. 2. Restart the app. 3. Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts. 4. Read the chip on the alert card.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-21.png: green chip 'mag 2.4  NAKED EYE' next to a card titled 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova'. DB: select id,kind,delta_mag,snr,fwhm from transient_detections -> 1|newSource|-2.35|18.4|2.41. There is no apparent-magnitude column on the table at all and photometric_transforms is empty, so 2.4 cannot be an apparent magnitude by construction.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a distinct deltaMag field to TransientAlert and leave `magnitude` null for First Light detections; render 'Δ 2.35 mag brighter' instead of 'mag 2.4', and suppress the brightness bucket entirely when only a delta is known.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Code, data and UI all check out. transient_alert_mapper.dart:20 is exactly 'final magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs();' and is passed straight into TransientAlert.magnitude, the apparent-magnitude field every alert surface consumes. transient_card.dart:580-588 _getBrightnessInfo buckets magnitude<=6 NAKED EYE / <=10 BINOCULAR / <=14 SMALL SCOPE, called at :532 and rendered as 'mag ${magnitude.toStringAsFixed(1)}' at :553. DB: transient_detections has exactly one row, kind=newSource delta_mag=-2.35 snr=18.4, and the table has no apparent-magnitude column at all, so 2.4 cannot be an apparent magnitude by construction. Confirmed live on my own profile: Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts renders 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova - Unconfirmed — possible new transient / mag 2.4 / NAKED EYE'. Because a difference-image delta larger than ~6 mag is essentially impossible, every First Light self-discovery with a measured delta is bucketed NAKED EYE or BINOCULAR. Cited file:line is precise.

findings.title: Confirming a First Light candidate does not update the Observing Alerts tab beside it: the same detection reads 'Confirmed' on one sub-tab and 'New' on the next
findings.what_happened: On Analytics > Science > First Light I pressed Confirm on the candidate; the card's badge changed to 'Confirmed', the toast read 'Marked as confirmed.' and the database row updated (reviewed=1). Switching one tab across to Observing Alerts -- the same screen, the same detection, mapped through transientAlertFromDetection -- the card still carries a blue 'New' badge and sits under the 'New' filter. transientAlertFromDetection maps reviewed -> TransientAlertState.acknowledged, so the alert list is being served from a snapshot taken at app launch and is not rebuilt when the detection changes.
findings.expected: Two views of one row, on two tabs of one screen, must not disagree. Confirming in First Light should immediately move the alert out of 'New'.
findings.repro: 1. Seed a confirmed-able detection and restart the app. 2. Analytics > Science > First Light > Confirm (badge becomes 'Confirmed', toast 'Marked as confirmed.'). 3. sqlite3 -> reviewed=1. 4. Click 'Observing Alerts'. 5. The card shows the 'New' badge.
findings.evidence: AT-SPI at 11:10 on First Light: 'Confirmed' twice plus 'panel: Marked as confirmed.'; DB at that instant: 1|newSource|1|0 (reviewed=1). /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-21.png at 11:14 on Observing Alerts: 'New' badge on the same detection. Mapping that should have produced 'acknowledged': packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/transients/transient_alert_mapper.dart:41-46.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/transient_alert_provider.dart (the alert list is not invalidated when transient_detections changes)
findings.proposed_fix: Have the alert provider watch the detections table (or invalidate it from the confirm/dismiss mutation) so both sub-tabs read one source of truth.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Symptom REPRODUCED LIVE on the rebuilt bundle: seeded detection id 1 (newSource, reviewed=0), Analytics > Science > First Light > Confirm -> DB reviewed=1 and the card badge reads 'Confirmed' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-12.png); one tab across, Observing Alerts shows the same detection ('NS J13.50+47.2', Supernova) with a blue 'New' badge (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-11.png). But the finding's cause and 'where' are wrong, which matters because the cited file is not the one to fix. transient_alert_mapper.dart:66-70 does map reviewed -> acknowledged, and the list IS rebuilt: activeTransientAlertsProvider is a StreamProvider.autoDispose holding `ref.listen(allTransientDetectionsProvider, ...)` (transient_alert_provider.dart:552-556), and allTransientDetectionsProvider is a drift watchRecentDetections live query (transient_detections_provider.dart:95-100) that re-emits on the local markReviewed write. The badge stays 'New' because the Observing Alerts UI never reads the alert's own state: transients_screen.dart:122 watches transientAlertStatesProvider, :143 does `states[alert.id]`, and transient_card.dart:56 falls back to newAlert when that map has no entry; _filterAlerts :167-172 puts exactly those under 'New'. That map is only ever populated from persisted `transient_alert_state_<id>` settings rows written by the user's own queue/dismiss actions (:683-810) -- nothing seeds it from TransientAlert.state, so the mapper's `acknowledged` is dead on this surface.
findings.location_wrong: Cause is packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/transients/transients_screen.dart:122/143/167-172 + widgets/transient_card.dart:56 (card state comes from transientAlertStatesProvider; TransientAlert.state is ignored), NOT 'transient_alert_provider.dart -- the alert list is not invalidated'; the list IS re-merged via ref.listen at transient_alert_provider.dart:552-556.

findings.title: The photometry 'Uncertainty' column mixes two units: magnitudes for target/check rows and raw ADU flux noise for every comparison-star row, ~3 million times larger
findings.what_happened: Analytics > Science > (export hub) > Photometry Measurements > CSV exports 495 rows with columns ... SNR, Uncertainty ... For target and check rows Uncertainty is a magnitude sigma (0.00054-0.00071 across all 198 such rows). For every one of the 297 comparison rows it is instead the flux noise in ADU (1912.7-2211.8). The identity is exact, not approximate: `select max(abs(uncertainty - flux/snr)) from photometry_measurements where role='comparison'` returns 0.0. So one column, in the database and in the CSV a user hands to AAVSO or plots error bars from, carries two physical quantities that differ by a factor of about 3.4 million, with no unit column to tell them apart.
findings.expected: Uncertainty must be a magnitude sigma for every row. A comparison star's uncertainty is 1.0857/SNR (or the same variance-propagated sigma the check star already gets); the ADU flux noise, if it is wanted, belongs in a separate `flux_uncertainty` column with its own header.
findings.repro: 1. Run a science session so photometry_measurements is populated (495 rows here). 2. Analytics > Science > toolbar database icon > Photometry Measurements > CSV. 3. Open the CSV: target/check rows have Uncertainty ~6e-4, comparison rows ~2.1e3. 4. Confirm in the DB: select role,count(*),min(uncertainty),max(uncertainty),max(abs(uncertainty-flux/snr)) from photometry_measurements group by role -> check|99|0.00056|0.00071|2354.4, comparison|297|1912.7|2211.8|0.0, target|99|0.00054|0.00068|2478.3.
findings.evidence: Exported file /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/photometry_2026-08-02T11-16-14.csv, e.g. image 100: target_primary flux 4629522 snr 2119.58 unc 0.000597 / comparison_2 flux 4506308 snr 2090.34 unc 2155.777 where flux/snr = 2155.777. Source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/science/science_processing_service/private_helpers.dart:465-471 `uncertainty: drift.Value<double?>(checkUncertainty ?? star.flux / (star.snr...))`.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the `?? star.flux / star.snr` fallback with a magnitude sigma (1.0857 / snr). Add a schema-level unit note and a test asserting every uncertainty in the table is < 1.0 magnitude.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced independently. private_helpers.dart:465-471 is exactly as cited: uncertainty: drift.Value<double?>(checkUncertainty ?? star.flux / (star.snr.isFinite ? star.snr.clamp(1.0,1e6).toDouble() : 1.0)). checkUncertainty is only non-null on the isCheck branch where it is 1.0857*sqrt(variance) — a magnitude sigma (lines 442-450) — so every comparison row falls through to flux/SNR, which is ADU flux noise. Verified in the scratch DB: group by role gives check|99|5.6e-4|7.1e-4, comparison|297|1912.68|2211.76 with max(abs(uncertainty - flux/snr)) = 0.0 exactly, target|99|5.4e-4|6.8e-4. Verified in the exported CSV /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/photometry_2026-08-02T11-16-14.csv: header 'Session ID,Image ID,Object ID,Role,X,Y,Flux,Differential Magnitude,SNR,Uncertainty,Is Outlier,Timestamp', column 10 is ~6e-4 for target/check and ~2e3 for comparison. One column, two physical quantities differing by ~3.4 million, no unit column. file:line correct.

findings.title: Science CSV exports never ask where to save and write to a hard-coded ~/Documents/Skotiq/exports, ignoring the app's configured data directory
findings.what_happened: Pressing CSV on 'Photometry Measurements' produced no save dialog at all; the toast read 'Exported 495 rows to /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/photometry_2026-08-02T11-16-14.csv'. findings.evidence: AT-SPI: 'Exported 495 rows to /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/photometry_2026-08-02T11-16-14.csv'. `ls /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/` shows the file plus artefacts from other audit profiles. The sandbox dir /tmp/ns-audit/r-science-review/ received nothing.

findings.verdict_reasoning: science_export_hub.dart:41-48 defines scienceExportDirectoryProvider as getApplicationDocumentsDirectory() + 'Skotiq/exports', created on demand; _exportData at :726-855 builds the CSV, reads that provider at :826, joins a timestamped filename and writes it with no picker anywhere in the path -- the only user-facing surface is the 'Exported N rows to <path>' string at :831. getApplicationDocumentsDirectory is path_provider's XDG documents dir, which nothing in the SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR / SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR plumbing overrides, so the export does ignore the configured data directory. The contrast the finding draws is real too: stack-result exports go through stackResultSavePickerProvider with a dialogTitle/fileName (stack_result_screen.dart:869-874). Location correct. Severity: P3 rather than P2 -- the file is written, the full path is reported in the result line, and on mobile revealExportedFile (:846) hands it to the share sheet; the harm is an unexpected location and a shared collision point, not lost data.

findings.title: The stack result's 'Avg HFR' statistic never renders because the service hard-codes avgHfr: null, even though every selected sub carries an HFR
findings.what_happened: stack_result_screen.dart:522 renders an 'Avg HFR ... px' row only `if (result.avgHfr != null)`, and stack_and_share_service.dart:425 persists `avgHfr: null` unconditionally. So the row is dead: two real Stack & Share runs in this session wrote stacked_results rows 2 and 3 with avg_hfr NULL, while every one of their source frames has hfr = 2.4 in captured_images. The only row in the table with an avg_hfr is one I seeded by hand. The result panel therefore shows Integration / Frames stacked / Rejected / Avg residual / Filter / Dimensions and silently omits the one number an imager actually judges a stack by.
findings.expected: Average the HFR of the frames that were integrated (they are already in hand as StackedFrameSelection rows) and persist it, so the panel shows 'Avg HFR 2.40 px'.
findings.repro: 1. Run Stack & Share to completion. 2. The result panel has no Avg HFR row. 3. sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select id,frames_stacked,avg_hfr from stacked_results' -> 2|7|(null), 3|8|(null); 'select distinct hfr from captured_images where session_id=3' -> 2.4.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-11.png (Integration panel with no HFR row). DB as above. Source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_and_share_service.dart:425 `avgHfr: null,`.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the mean HFR over the frames whose add succeeded and pass it in place of the null.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Both cited lines are exact in the current tree. stack_and_share_service.dart:425 is `avgHfr: null,` (unconditional, in the single StackAndShareResult the run persists) and stack_result_screen.dart:522 is `if (result.avgHfr != null)` guarding the 'Avg HFR' _StatRow. No other local producer sets it -- the only other references are stacking_operations.dart:251 reading it back off a remote host's JSON (fed by this same null on the host) and stacked_results_dao.dart:164 reading the column. So on the local path the column is always NULL and the row can never render. The source now carries a justification comment ('the live-stacking engine does not measure HFR ... a later analysis pass may populate it'), so it is a known gap rather than an oversight, but the factual claim -- dead UI row, hard-coded null -- holds and the file:line is right. P3 correct.

findings.title: The five-rung Science guide is a set of paragraphs, not a ladder you can climb -- every rung opens an explanation and a 'Got it' button with no action
findings.what_happened: Analytics > Science shows a 'Science guide' with rungs 1-5 (Measure your sky / Track a star / Build a light curve / Find the period / Contribute it) and a single page-level 'Run calibration' button. Opening rung 2 gives 'Point at a target and let the photometry follow it frame to frame...' plus the gate 'Calibrate your sky first so brightness reads true.' and one button: 'Got it'. Rung 5 gives 'Your measurements are good enough to share...' plus 'Find a period - or build out the curve - before exporting.' and again only 'Got it'. Neither sheet offers the action it is describing, or a link to where that action lives. The only actionable rung is rung 1, whose button is on the page rather than in the sheet.
findings.expected: Each rung sheet should carry the action for that rung -- 'Pick a target' (rung 2), 'Open the light curve' (rung 3), 'Run period search' (rung 4), 'Open the export hub' (rung 5) -- enabled or disabled with the stated prerequisite. As built, a user who reads the ladder has to go find each surface themselves, which is exactly the discoverability problem the ladder exists to solve.
findings.repro: 1. Analytics > Science. 2. Click rung 2 'Track a star' -> sheet with text and 'Got it'. 3. Escape, click rung 5 'Contribute it' -> sheet with text and 'Got it'.
findings.evidence: AT-SPI of the rung-2 sheet: 'panel: Track a star / Point at a target and let the photometry follow it frame to frame... / Calibrate your sky first so brightness reads true. / button: Got it'. Rung 5: '...Export them for the AAVSO or the MPC... / Find a period - or build out the curve - before exporting. / button: Got it'. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-23.png shows the ladder and the lone 'Run calibration'.
findings.proposed_fix: Give ScienceRungSheet a primary action per rung that routes to that rung's surface, disabled with the prerequisite as its tooltip when the gate is unmet.

findings.title: The standalone /science route can never build ScienceScreen -- its redirect always fires, so the screen class and its Scaffold are unreachable code
findings.what_happened: app_router.dart declares the /science GoRoute with BOTH a `redirect` that unconditionally returns '/analytics?tab=science...' and a `pageBuilder` that constructs ScienceScreen. In go_router a non-null redirect short-circuits the route, so the pageBuilder never runs. ScienceScreen is constructed in exactly one place in the whole repo -- that dead pageBuilder -- so the class, its Scaffold and its initialTabQuery plumbing ship but can never appear. Driving the app confirms it: every route into science lands on the Analytics shell with the Science tab selected, never on a standalone science screen.
findings.expected: Delete the dead pageBuilder (and ScienceScreen with it) or drop the redirect if a standalone screen is actually wanted. Leaving both is a trap: a future reader editing ScienceScreen will change nothing that ships.
findings.repro: 1. Reach science by every available path -- Dashboard cockpit narrator, imaging science HUD, sequencer light-curve panel, transients screen. 2. All land on Analytics with the Science tab active (header reads 'Analytics', sub-tabs Science / First Light / Observing Alerts). 3. grep -rn 'ScienceScreen' packages apps --include='*.dart' -> only the definition and app_router.dart:232.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-23.png (the only rendering of the science workspace is inside the Analytics shell). packages/skotiq_app/lib/router/app_router.dart:222-236: `redirect: (context, state) { ... return '/analytics?tab=science...'; }` followed by `pageBuilder: ... child: ScienceScreen(initialTabQuery: tabQuery)`.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the pageBuilder from the /science route and delete ScienceScreen, keeping ScienceWorkspaceView as the single implementation.
findings.verdict_reasoning: app_router.dart:222-236 is exactly as described: the '/science' GoRoute declares `redirect: (context, state) { final sub = state.uri.queryParameters['tab']; return '/analytics?tab=science...'; }` -- an unconditional non-null return -- followed by a pageBuilder constructing ScienceScreen. go_router short-circuits a route whose redirect returns non-null, so the pageBuilder is unreachable. app_router.dart:232 is the only construction of ScienceScreen in packages/ or apps/ (other hits are the definition at science_screen.dart:246/249 and a doc comment at :42). Corroborated live: navigating to Science lands on the Analytics shell with sub-tabs Science / First Light / Observing Alerts (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-08.png), never a standalone screen. Cited locations exact; P3 is generous (cost is dead code plus the trap it sets) but not wrong.
